subject: Shipped: The People Graph 360° presentation surface

body.summary: 22-slide editorial presentation of Eglin's people-graph research brief. Built as a standalone surface — someone who has not read the long-form artifact leaves understanding the people-graph thesis. Stripe Press aesthetic, one idea per slide, full keyboard navigation, grid overview, hash routing.

arc: 01 Cover (Fraunces on ink, rt-stamp, cover meta)
02 Thesis (canonical pull quote on dark bg)
03 Definition (5 properties as a labeled list)
04 What it is not — part 1 (HRIS / ATS / org chart)
05 What it is not — part 2 (LinkedIn / Microsoft Graph)
06–09 Four era cards (payroll-first through point-solution explosion)
10 Competitor scan: Shipped (Gloat, Beamery, LinkedIn, Microsoft)
12 Competitor scan: Claim (HiBob, Rippling, Lattice, Eqtble/Deel, Mercor out-of-scope)
13 Why agentic companies need a graph (5-reason grid on indigo-deep bg)
18 Architecture: graph vs. warehouse comparison (2-column, preserves ASCII art logic)
21 Stratum implications (3-card grid, Tier-2 framing, on dark bg)

navigation.keyboard: Left/right and up/down arrows advance/retreat slides
navigation.onscreen: Fixed bottom nav bar: Prev button, slide counter (N / 22), slide title, Next button, Grid button
navigation.grid_overview: G key opens full-page thumbnail grid; Esc closes it; clicking any thumbnail jumps to that slide
navigation.hash_routing: URL updates to #N on each slide change; browser Back/Forward work; direct deep-links (presentation.html#7) work on load
navigation.touch: Horizontal swipe left/right advances/retreats on mobile
navigation.screen_reader: aria-live polite region announces slide change ('Slide N of 22: [title]'); focus moves to slide heading on advance; skip-to-first-slide link

discovery.from_research_artifact: Small 'View as presentation ↗' link added below the masthead in people-graph-360.html (before the TOC), styled as .pres-link in mono uppercase
discovery.from_homepage_card: Secondary 'View as presentation →' CTA added beside the existing 'Read the research →' link in the research section of index.html, tinted indigo to distinguish from primary ochre CTA

design.typography: Fraunces (display/headings), Newsreader (body), JetBrains Mono (labels, meta, pills)
design.palette: paper / ink / ochre / moss / plum / indigo — indigo is the research accent, more prominent here than in the long-form
design.slide_themes: light (default) / warm / dark (ink bg) / deep (indigo-deep bg) / vignette (paper-warm + indigo top-border)
design.print_path: page-break-after: always per slide; dark slides use color-adjust: exact

contrast_verified: indigo (#3d4d7d) on paper: 6.99:1 — used ONLY for large heading em (slide__h2 em, thesis quote em, era-rule decorative): large-text AAA threshold is 4.5:1, PASS
plum on paper (counter nums): 7.67:1 AAA PASS
paper on ink (cover/dark body): 15.38:1 AAA PASS
ochre-soft on ink (cover em): 11.20:1 AAA PASS
paper on indigo-deep (deep slide body): 10.11:1 AAA PASS
p-shipped pill text (#3a4a2c, deep moss) on paper: 8.13:1 AAA PASS — upgraded from var(--moss) which was 6.12:1
vignette after label (#3a4a2c) on paper-warm: 8.42:1 AAA PASS
accessibility.motion: prefers-reduced-motion: reduce disables all CSS transitions and uses auto scroll behavior in JS
accessibility.keyboard: Full keyboard walkthrough implemented; focus moves to slide heading on advance; no keyboard trap; Esc in grid mode closes grid and returns focus to grid button
accessibility.aria_live: polite region announces slide changes; nav counter also aria-live

known_issues: No og:image / social card image generated — if a CHRO shares this URL in LinkedIn the preview will be text-only. Low priority; can be addressed with a static PNG thumbnail in a future pass.

Grid thumbnail previews are text-only (not miniaturized slide renders) — CSS scaling trick to preview actual slide content would require either server-side rendering or a canvas-capture approach. Current approach is clean and accessible.
The homepage research-cta secondary link uses an inline style for the indigo color — should be moved to a named CSS class (.research-cta--secondary or similar) in a future design system pass.
